key_insight: An ultrafast plenoptic camera can reconstruct individual charged-particle tracks in 3D from photon-starved, single-event scintillator images.
engineering_relevance: This enables high-resolution particle tracking in unsegmented detector volumes, reducing the need for extremely fine physical segmentation.
method: Calibrated the PLATON plenoptic SPAD-array prototype with laser-induced scintillation tracks in plastic scintillator.
Used a novel reconstruction algorithm to recover 3D photon-starved line trajectories.
Validated performance against custom Monte Carlo simulation and then test-beam pion data at CERN.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports good agreement with custom Monte Carlo simulations and successful event-by-event reconstruction of 3D pion tracks from 2D photon-starved images.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated on a prototype and controlled test-beam setup, so robustness in larger-scale detector systems and higher-background conditions still needs verification.
paper_title: Event-by-event track imaging of charged particles with an ultrafast plenoptic camera
